source.title: The Growth Order of a Solution of a Singular Non-Self-Adjoint Differential Equation, as a Function of the Spectral Parameter

accepted.question_text: Consider the differential equation iε d/dx(f(x) du/dx) + i du/dx = λu, where f(x) is positive on (0, π), f'(0)=1, and f extends to a 2π-periodic odd C²-function on ℝ. For each λ ∈ ℂ, let ψ(x, λ) denote the unique solution normalized by lim_{x→0} ψ(x, λ) = 1. For a fixed spatial point x ∈ (0, π], what is the growth order of ψ(x, λ), viewed as an analytic function of the spectral parameter λ?
accepted.context_brief: Growth order for solutions of a singular non-self-adjoint differential equation

evidence.quote: A generalization of this work [2] considers the differential equation i d/dx f(x) du/dx + i du/dx = λu, in which f(x) > 0 on (0, π), f'(0) = 1, and f has (say) a C2(R) 2π-periodic odd extension to the whole real line.
It is known that there exists, for each λ ∈ C, a unique solution of the differential equation, say ψ(x, λ), with the properties lim x→0 ψ(x, λ)=1
Open problem: for fixed x ∈ (0, π], what is the growth order of ψ(x, λ) as an analytic function of λ?

accepted.question_text: For a Schrödinger equation on the real line with a PT-symmetric potential, suppose there are two distinguished solutions ψleft(x, λ) ∈ L²(−∞, 0) and ψright(x, λ) ∈ L²(0, ∞) for the spectral parameter λ; these may be taken as Jost solutions when the potential lies in L¹(ℝ). After normalizing these half-line solutions in an appropriate way, what can be said about their growth orders as functions of λ?
accepted.context_brief: Growth orders of normalized half-line solutions for PT-symmetric Schrödinger equations

evidence.quote: A similar problem arises in consideration of Schrödinger equations with PT-symmetric potentials on the real line. Here one has two solutions ψleft(x, λ) ∈ L2(−∞, 0) and ψright(x, λ) ∈ L2(0,∞), Jost solutions, for instance, if the potential lies in L1(R).
Normalizing these solutions in some appropriate way, what can one say about their growth orders?
